newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisian President urges watch on food market data.
newsitem.headline: Tunisian President urges watch on food market data.

text.p: Tunisian President Zine al-Abidine Ben Ali on Monday asked the country's operators to watch closely data on food commodities on world markets, saying it was necessary for the country's food security.

"The fluctuations in the world's markets of agriculture products and the intensification of competition between the main economic groupings impose on us the imperative duty of closely outwatching the data related to," Ben Ali said in a speech at the occasion of the Agriculture Day.
"Their developments must be analysed and prospects explored, in the aim of not beeing caught by the fluctuations of prices and the tendencies of the offer and demand," he added.
He said the outwatch would permit to explore favourable opportunities for the country's agriculture and "food and economic security."

Ben Ali also said that his country would encourage further foreign investments in the country's agriculture sector, mainly by easing procedures. He did not elaborate but said a draft law would be submitted soon to the parliament.

He also encouraged the private sector to invest in seeds of cereals and other agricultural products for which he asked the government to prepare a plan aimed at "rationalising" their import, encouraging the private sector, and modernising the sector.
